title: Stackification of groupoids: local objects, isomorphisms and extension
statement: Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-topos] small in the larger universe, with fibre groupoids and their morphism sets in that universe. A category fibred in groupoids $\mathcal P$ on $\mathcal C$ has pullback objects along every base arrow, unique up to the usual cartesian isomorphisms. A $J$-stack means that isomorphism presheaves on slice sites are $J$-sheaves and all covering descent data for objects are effective. There exist a $J$-stack $a_J\mathcal P$ and a pullback-compatible functor $i:\mathcal P\to a_J\mathcal P$ with the following properties. For every $T\in\mathcal C$ and $u,v\in\mathcal P(T)$, the isomorphism sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}(i(u),i(v))$ is the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal P}(u,v)$. Every object of $(a_J\mathcal P)(T)$ belongs locally on a $J$-covering of $T$ to the essential image of $i$. For every $J$-stack $\mathcal Y$ and pullback-compatible functor $F:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Y$, there exist a pullback-compatible functor $\bar F:a_J\mathcal P\to\mathcal Y$ and an invertible natural transformation $\bar F i\cong F$. These assertions apply also to the category fibred in groupoids associated to a presheaf of groupoids. The notation $a_J\mathcal P$ denotes a stackification with these properties.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-morphism-sheafification] to obtain $q:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q=\mathcal P^{\mathrm{pre}}$. Thus $\mathcal Q$ is a prestack with exactly the same fibre objects, and its isomorphism sheaves are the sheafifications of those of $\mathcal P$. Apply [lem-sfb-prestack-sieve-descent-completion] to this prestack and set $a_J\mathcal P=\mathcal D\mathcal Q$ and $i=e q$. The cited construction makes this a stack and $i$ pullback-compatible.

The fibrewise full faithfulness of $e$ identifies $\operatorname{Isom}(i(u),i(v))$ with $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Q}(q(u),q(v))$, compatibly on every slice restriction. The latter is $I_{u,v}^{\#}$ by the morphism-sheafification node. For an object $(R,x)$ of the completion, every $f:V\to T$ in its covering sieve gives $(R,x)|_V\cong e(x_f)$. Since $q$ is identity on objects, each $x_f$ is $q(u_f)$ for an object of $\mathcal P(V)$. These are precisely the required local representatives.

Let $F:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Y$ with $\mathcal Y$ a stack. It is a prestack, so the morphism-sheafification node gives $G:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Y$ and $Gq\cong F$. For $A=(R,x)$, apply $G$ to the cartesian section $x$. Effectivity of descent in $\mathcal Y$ gives an object $y_A\in\mathcal Y(T)$ with identifications $y_A|_V\cong G(x_f)$ compatible for all $f:V\to T$ in $R$. Choose these objects and identifications. An arrow $A\to B$ is represented on a common covering subsieve $K$ by a compatible family $\alpha_f:x_f\to z_f$. Conjugating $G(\alpha_f)$ by the chosen identifications gives a matching family of arrows $y_A|_V\to y_B|_V$. The isomorphism sheaf of $\mathcal Y$ glues it uniquely to $\bar F(\alpha):y_A\to y_B$. Representatives equal on a covering refinement give the same glued arrow; composition and identities hold because they hold after restriction to a common covering subsieve. Hence this defines fibre functors.

For a base arrow $h:V\to T$, both $h^*y_A$ and $y_{h^*A}$ are realizations of the section $G(x)$ pulled back to $h^*R$. Their specified identifications give a unique comparison isomorphism, by the isomorphism-sheaf axiom of $\mathcal Y$. The identity and composition comparisons agree on covering sieves, where they are the comparisons for $G$, hence agree globally. Define the functor on arrows over $h$ by factoring them as a vertical arrow followed by a cartesian lift and using this comparison; its coherence gives a pullback-compatible $\bar F$. For $A=e(u)$ the maximal-sieve section is the pullback section of $u$, so $y_{e(u)}\cong G(u)$ by the same unique gluing. The construction of arrows makes these isomorphisms natural, giving $\bar F e\cong G$ and $\bar F i\cong Gq\cong F$. All descent and comparison assertions here use the defining stack axioms of $\mathcal Y$, not a uniqueness assertion absent from the supporting nodes.

For a presheaf of groupoids $P$, its associated fibred groupoid has objects $(T,u)$, $u\in P(T)$; an arrow over $h:V\to T$ from $(V,v)$ to $(T,u)$ is an isomorphism $v\to P(h)(u)$. Identity and composition use those of $P$, and the identity of $P(h)(u)$ supplies a cartesian lift. Thus it meets the same hypotheses, and the construction above applies.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q109-6b107ed63 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the source in full: stacks.tex lemma-stackify 02ZN (naive and less-naive proofs), 0435 with its hint, 02ZP (1),(2) and 0436. The item statement is unchanged from the base (byte-identical to every Q79 snapshot). New node lem-sfb-groupoid-morphism-sheafification is true. It keeps the objects and sheafifies the Isom presheaves (sheafification commutes with slice restriction and finite products), gives a prestack with q the identity on objects, and extends functors into prestacks because Isom_Z is a sheaf. New node lem-sfb-prestack-sieve-descent-completion is true. Its transitions between covering subsieves are bijective for a prestack, so the Hom colimit is well defined. e is fibrewise fully faithful through maximal sieves, the Isom sheaves glue over the composite sieve, object descent is effective via the generated sieve, and (R,x)|_V ≅ e(x_f) because f^*R is maximal. With an empty sieve the fibre is contractible. Both new nodes are statement-only, self-contained, carry tags and labels, have their searches recorded, and are not leaves (Mathlib has no stackification). rg -L over the DAG and blueprint_refs search found no duplicates. Neither node restates the item: node 1 adds no objects; node 2 assumes a prestack and has no universal property. Steps: 1 composes the two nodes (node 2's sole hypothesis comes from node 1). 2 is elementary: full faithfulness plus pullback compatibility give Isom = I^#, and local representatives are e(q(u_f)). 3 and 4 write out the extension that 0435 omits: effectivity in Y, conjugated matching families glued in Isom_Y, independence of representatives by separatedness, pullback comparisons glued uniquely, and F̄e ≅ G. 5 is the elementary Grothendieck construction. Small cases checked: trivial topology, a discrete non-sheaf fibred groupoid (node 2 essential), BG (sheafify G, then torsors), and ∅ ∈ J. No SGA cited, route unchanged, no tool_uses. Advisory: the slice-site topology is used without a definition node (already so in the base statement), and Y in the item should be read as a stack in groupoids as in 0436. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_groupoid_stackification_local_description {C : Type w} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (P : Pseudofunctor (LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ) Cat.{w, w}) (hP : ∀ T : C, IsGroupoid (P.obj (.mk (op T)))) : ∃ A : Pseudofunctor (LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ) Cat.{w, w}, (∀ T : C, IsGroupoid (A.obj (.mk (op T)))) ∧ A.IsStack J ∧ ∃ i : StrongTrans P A, (∀ (T : C) (u v : P.obj (.mk (op T))), ∃ e : sheafify (J.over T) (P.presheafHom u v) ≅ A.presheafHom ((i.app (.mk (op T))).toFunctor.obj u) ((i.app (.mk (op T))).toFunctor.obj v), ∀ (V : Over T) (φ : (P.presheafHom u v).obj (op V)), e.hom.app (op V) ((toSheafify (J.over T) (P.presheafHom u v)).app (op V) φ) = (i.naturality V.hom.op.toLoc).inv.toNatTrans.app u ≫ (i.app (.mk (op V.left))).toFunctor.map φ ≫ (i.naturality V.hom.op.toLoc).hom.toNatTrans.app v) ∧ (∀ (T : C) (a : A.obj (.mk (op T))), ∃ R : Sieve T, R ∈ J T ∧ ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ T), R f → ∃ u : P.obj (.mk (op V)), Nonempty ((i.app (.mk (op V))).toFunctor.obj u ≅ (A.map f.op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj a)) ∧ (∀ (Y : Pseudofunctor (LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ) Cat.{w, w}), (∀ T : C, IsGroupoid (Y.obj (.mk (op T)))) → Y.IsStack J → ∀ F : StrongTrans P Y, ∃ H : StrongTrans A Y, Nonempty (@CategoryTheory.Iso (StrongTrans P Y) (StrongTrans.homCategory (F := P) (G := Y)) (StrongTrans.vcomp i H) F))
